title: Null pointers, null pointer constants and safe checks
learningObjectives: Explain what a null pointer represents in C.
Use NULL or an appropriate null pointer constant to initialize pointer objects.
Compare pointers with NULL before dereferencing when null is an allowed state.
Distinguish a null pointer value from an all-bits-zero object representation.
Recognize that a non-null pointer is not automatically valid or safe to dereference.

understand.concept: A null pointer value is guaranteed to compare unequal to a pointer to any object or function. The macro NULL expands to an implementation-defined null pointer constant. A null pointer can be checked before dereferencing when null is an allowed state. The language does not require a null pointer to have an all-bits-zero representation, and non-nullness alone does not prove that a pointer is valid.
understand.whyItMatters: This knowledge helps reason about C data representation, object bounds and valid memory access.
understand.analogy: Think of memory objects as labelled storage and pointers as typed references to that storage.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal pointer, lifetime and object-access rules.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Meaning of null

A null pointer represents the absence of a pointer to an object or function. It is a special pointer value, not an object located at a universally fixed numeric address.

## 2. Initialize and compare

Use `NULL` or another appropriate null pointer constant to initialize a pointer. Compare a pointer with NULL to check whether it currently has no target. The pointer must not be dereferenced while null.

## 3. Representation is not the same as value

C guarantees the behavior of null pointer values, but it does not require every implementation to represent them as all bits zero. Do not use memset or integer assumptions as a substitute for proper pointer initialization.

## 4. A non-null pointer may still be invalid

A pointer can be non-null but dangling, out of bounds, misaligned or otherwise invalid. A null check only handles one possible invalid state; it does not establish object lifetime or bounds.

## 5. Establish pointer contracts

Document whether a function accepts NULL, whether it may return NULL, and which object the pointer may designate. Validate all required preconditions before dereferencing.

examples.title: Check a nullable pointer
examples.explanation: The pointer is initialized to a null pointer value and checked before any dereference.

examples.title: Check before dereferencing
examples.explanation: The function defines how it handles a null argument. A non-null pointer must still designate a valid live int object.

practise.guidedTask: Write a C program demonstrating CL5.7. State the relevant input, pointer or conversion contract, then compile and trace the normal and failure paths.
practise.independentTask: Create a second example for CL5.7 that exercises a boundary or invalid state. Add checks, document the ownership or input rules, and explain why unsafe behavior is avoided.
hints: Read the declared types carefully, including every pointer and qualifier level.
Check return values and validate inputs before use.
Keep object lifetime and ownership explicit.
Avoid dereferencing invalid or out-of-range pointers.
Test both success and failure paths.

questions.prompt: What does a null pointer represent?
options: A pointer value that designates no object or function
A pointer to the integer zero object
A guaranteed address with all bits zero
questions.answer: A pointer value that designates no object or function
questions.explanation: Null is a special pointer value that designates no target.

options: A macro that expands to an implementation-defined null pointer constant
A pointer to the first array element
questions.answer: A macro that expands to an implementation-defined null pointer constant
questions.explanation: NULL is provided by standard headers as a null pointer constant.

questions.prompt: Must a null pointer have an all-bits-zero representation?
questions.explanation: The C standard specifies null pointer behavior, not a universal bit representation.

questions.prompt: Does a non-null pointer guarantee safe dereferencing?
options: No; it may be dangling or out of bounds
Yes, every non-null pointer is valid
questions.answer: No; it may be dangling or out of bounds
questions.explanation: Pointer validity also depends on object lifetime, bounds and alignment.

questions.prompt: What must a program do before dereferencing a pointer that may be null?
options: Check it and establish the other pointer validity requirements
questions.answer: Check it and establish the other pointer validity requirements
questions.explanation: A null check handles the null case, but the target must also be valid.
